concepts.name: Historical Injustice Framework and Constitutional Basis of FRA
key_dimensions: FRA as a corrective legislation addressing colonial-era dispossession under Indian Forest Act 1927
Constitutional backing via Articles 21, 46, and Fifth/Sixth Schedule provisions
FRA as recognition of pre-existing rights vs. grant of new rights — a critical legal distinction
Relationship with PESA 1996 and how FRA extends/complements gram sabha powers

concepts.name: Definition and Scope of 'Forest Dweller' under FRA
key_dimensions: Two categories: Scheduled Tribes (ST) and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (OTFD) — eligibility criteria differences
75-year residency cut-off requirement for OTFDs and its evidentiary challenges
Primitive Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) and their special recognition under FRA
Pastoral and nomadic communities — inclusion controversies and practical exclusions

concepts.name: Individual Forest Rights (IFR) — Scope, Limits and Pattas
key_dimensions: IFR covers land under cultivation prior to 13 December 2005 — significance of this cut-off date
Maximum ceiling of 4 hectares per family and non-alienability/non-transferability clause
Rights are heritable but NOT transferable — common UPSC trap point
Difference between IFR pattas and revenue land titles — IFR does not confer ownership but usufructuary rights

concepts.name: Community Forest Rights (CFR) — Nature and Extent
key_dimensions: CFR covers nistar rights, grazing, fishing, water bodies, community tenures, and habitat rights
Distinction between Community Forest Rights and Community Forest Resource (CFR-R) management rights
CFR-R empowers gram sabha to manage, protect, and conserve forest resources — a governance shift
Overlap and conflicts with Joint Forest Management (JFM) committees under Forest Department

concepts.name: Habitat Rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)
key_dimensions: Habitat rights are collective rights over customary habitat, distinct from individual and community rights
Recognition includes areas used for seasonal resource use, shifting cultivation, and sacred groves
Only PVTGs (75 groups notified) are eligible — not all STs qualify automatically
Implementation gap: very few habitat rights have been formally recognized despite legal provision

concepts.name: Rights over Minor Forest Produce (MFP) — Definition and Ownership
key_dimensions: FRA 2006 grants ownership rights over MFP, not merely collection rights — a paradigm shift
MFP includes all non-timber forest produce of plant origin: bamboo, tendu, honey, medicinal plants etc.
Bamboo was reclassified from timber to MFP under Indian Forest Act amendment 2017 — UPSC link
Conflict between State Forest Development Corporations' monopoly on MFP and FRA ownership rights

concepts.name: Gram Sabha as the Primary Authority — Powers and Process
key_dimensions: Gram Sabha is the initiating authority for claims — not the Forest Department or Revenue Department
Three-tier structure: Gram Sabha → Sub-Divisional Level Committee → District Level Committee
Gram Sabha can reject, modify, or approve claims; higher committees can only examine, not override gram sabha
Quorum requirement and role of women members (one-third representation mandatory in committees)

concepts.name: Forest Rights Committees (FRC) — Composition and Functioning
key_dimensions: FRC is constituted by gram sabha — minimum 10 to maximum 15 members with mandatory one-third women
FRC prepares claim maps using participatory GIS and community surveys
FRC is NOT a government body — it is a community body under gram sabha authority
Common trap: FRC recommends, gram sabha decides — confusion between the two roles in exam questions

concepts.name: Diversion of Forest Land and FPIC under FRA
key_dimensions: Section 5 and Rule 4(5): No diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes without gram sabha consent
Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) — FRA's implicit requirement aligned with UNDRIP principles
Supreme Court's Vedanta-Niyamgiri judgment (2013) operationalizing gram sabha veto on mining
Distinction between Section 5 rights (protective) and consent for diversion — often confused in questions

concepts.name: Resettlement and Relocation Provisions under FRA
key_dimensions: Section 4(2): No eviction or relocation until rights are recognized and resettlement conditions are met
Resettlement requires free informed consent, alternative land, and livelihood support — all three mandatory
Critical Tigre Reserve vs. Forest Rights conflict: wildlife corridors and Section 38V of Wildlife Protection Act
2019 Supreme Court eviction order controversy — highlighting implementation gaps and state non-compliance

concepts.name: FRA and Protected Areas — National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries and Tiger Reserves
key_dimensions: FRA rights are applicable even inside National Parks and Sanctuaries — common misconception that they are excluded
Critical Wildlife Habitat (CWH) declaration process requires settlement of rights BEFORE notification
Conflict between Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (pre-FRA) and FRA 2006 — FRA is a later, special law
Project Tiger and NTCA guidelines vs. FRA gram sabha consent requirements — institutional conflict

concepts.name: Rights of Shifting Cultivators (Podu/Jhum) under FRA
key_dimensions: FRA recognizes rights of shifting cultivators including areas fallowed under rotation — important inclusion
Challenge: shifting cultivation is not 'settled' cultivation — mapping and documentation difficulties
States like Odisha, Jharkhand, Northeast states have differing approaches to jhum rights recognition
Interaction with Forest Conservation Act 1980: jhum land classified as degraded forest — legal ambiguity

concepts.name: Nodal Agencies and Implementation Architecture
key_dimensions: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) is the nodal ministry — NOT the Ministry of Environment, a key trap
State-level monitoring committee chaired by Chief Secretary — multi-ministry coordination requirement
District Collector chairs the District Level Committee (DLC) — the final authority on individual claims
Forest Department's role is advisory at DLC level — they do NOT have veto power, contrary to practice

concepts.name: Rejection of Claims — Procedural Safeguards and Grounds
key_dimensions: Claims can only be rejected with written reasons by DLC — oral or summary rejections are illegal
Rejected claimants have right to appeal to Sub-Divisional Level Committee and then DLC
State governments cannot issue blanket rejection orders — must be case-by-case (SC guidelines)
Mass rejection controversy: multiple states rejected millions of claims citing insufficient evidence — 2019 SC case

concepts.name: FRA and Forest Conservation Act (FCA) 1980 — Interface and Conflicts
key_dimensions: FCA 1980 requires central government approval for any non-forest use of forest land
FRA 2006 exempts small-scale developmental activities by gram sabha from FCA clearance (Section 3(2))
Section 3(2) facilities include schools, hospitals, roads up to certain limits — without FCA clearance
Post-Forest Conservation Amendment Act 2023 — new tensions with FRA gram sabha rights over deemed forests

concepts.name: Recognition of Rights over Traditionally Protected Forests and Sacred Groves
key_dimensions: FRA recognizes rights over community conserved areas and sacred groves (devvans, orans, etc.)
Sacred groves may be within revenue land or forest land — jurisdictional complexity
Rights over traditional conservation by tribals vs. state's forest management paradigm — power conflict
Biodiversity Act 2002 overlap: Community Biodiversity Registers and FRA CFR rights — complementary framework

concepts.name: FRA and Compensatory Afforestation — CAMPA Linkage
key_dimensions: CAMPA funds used for afforestation on 'degraded forest land' — often overlaps with areas where FRA rights exist
Plantation drives on FRA-eligible land without rights recognition — de facto eviction through greening
Eco-sensitive zones and buffer zone plantations conflicting with community forest resource management
Parliamentary Standing Committee observations on CAMPA-FRA coordination failures

concepts.name: FRA Implementation Data — Progress, Gaps and State-wise Disparities
key_dimensions: Titles issued vs. claims filed ratio — national average below 50%, with significant state variation
Odisha and Chhattisgarh as relative success stories vs. Gujarat and Maharashtra controversies
CFR recognition significantly lagging behind IFR — structural bias toward individual over community rights
MoTA annual reports data used in UPSC mains — awareness of approximate figures and trends expected

concepts.name: Judicial Pronouncements on FRA — Key Cases
key_dimensions: Wildlife First vs. MoTA (2019): SC ordered eviction of 10 lakh families — later stayed, highlighting implementation crisis
Niyamgiri case (Vedanta Resources vs. State of Odisha, 2013): gram sabha veto on mining upheld
Samata judgment (1997) — pre-FRA but foundational for tribal land alienation jurisprudence
High Court rulings on state governments bypassing gram sabha consent — pattern of executive overreach

concepts.name: FRA vs. Land Acquisition Act 2013 — Interplay in Tribal Areas
key_dimensions: LARR 2013 requires 80% consent for tribal land acquisition — FRA adds gram sabha consent layer
Double consent requirement: LARR consent + FRA gram sabha FPIC for forest land in tribal areas
Linear projects (roads, railways, pipelines) in forest areas — which law takes precedence?
Fifth Schedule areas: Governor's powers, PESA, FRA and LARR — layered protection often tested in GS2/GS3 overlap
